Upset sale date: bureau schedules sale no earlier than the second Monday of September and before October 1; sale may be adjourned.

No owner-occupied property may be sold at upset sale unless the bureau gave the owner-occupant written notice at least 10 days before the sale by personal service by the sheriff or deputy (or person appointed by county commissioners).

If no bid equal to the upset price is received, the sale continues without further advertisement so the bureau may sell at private sale or petition court for an order to sell free and discharged of liens (judicial sale).

Within 30 days of presentation of the consolidated return the court confirms sales nisi if regularly conducted; bureau must notify each owner by certified restricted-delivery mail within 30 days of the actual sale of the right to file objections within 30 days after confirmation nisi.
RETSL 'actual sale' means payment of the full amount agreed by the successful upset-sale bidder (sections 605-609).
The Pennsylvania Supreme Court (2026) held that due process requires at minimum that an owner receive notice prior to an upset sale.
